title: Generic resource graph move envelope
goal: Collapse bespoke machinen move envelopes into a generic resource-class envelope so any binary whose observed resource graph is fully understood can be moved target-native without app-specific code, while unsupported resource classes fail closed with exact evidence and no target pid.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove the product contract for 'fully understood resource graph' is documented, including supported/refused/unknown/deferred resource statuses, loader strategies, success evidence, refusal evidence, and explicit non-goals such as arbitrary memory teleportation, source-ISA emulation, and metadata-only success.
proofChecklist.evidence: Documented the generic resource graph product contract in docs/snapshot/generic-resource-graph-move.md and linked it from docs/snapshot/README.md. The doc defines the slogan "Support any binary whose resource graph is fully understood", resource graph semantics, status values supported/refused/unknown/deferred/ignorable, loader strategies reexec/target-native-restart/brokered-fd/continuation, success evidence, refusal evidence, first generic target, initial supported classes, initial refused/deferred classes, frontier resource classes, and non-goals including arbitrary memory/process/ELF/runtime restore, source-ISA emulation success, metadata-only success, blind execve replay, and hiding unsupported pipes/PTys/sockets/mmap/epoll/locks/timers/runtime state behind an accepted descriptor.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove existing proven move envelopes are inventoried and mapped to normalized resource classes so the generic envelope is grounded in already-graduated behavior rather than starting from scratch.
proofChecklist.evidence: Inventoried existing proven move matrix rows in docs/snapshot/generic-resource-graph-inventory.json. The inventory maps current scripts/smoke/move-envelope-matrix.sh PROOF_NAMES into normalized resource classes including processIdentity, argvEnvCwd, regularFileIdentity, directoryIdentity, filesystemMutation, atomicOutput, archiveMemberPolicy, loopbackTcpListener, noActiveClients, serviceConfigIdentity, dataDirIdentity, databaseSafety, healthProbe, unsupportedResourceRefusal, runtimeSpecificRefusal, and terminalOrPtyRefusal. This proves the generic envelope is grounded in all current matrix proof names instead of starting from scratch.

stopIf: The implementation would claim arbitrary binary/process teleportation without proving every observed resource class in the graph.
The implementation would use source-ISA emulation as success instead of target-native reconstruction or explicit refusal.
The implementation would let a target loader launch before all generic resource graph preflight gates pass.
The implementation would hide unsupported resources behind metadata-only success or a broad catch-all accepted state.
The implementation would regress existing proven bespoke envelope support or refusal evidence without an equivalent generic proof.
The implementation would bake proof-only tools into base assets instead of provisioning them in proof VMs or disposable overlays.
Required local VMM assets, proof packages, or remote amd64 access are unavailable for the proof being claimed.
A required validation command fails and cannot be fixed within the current goal scope.
The /goal loop reaches 8 agent completion(s) without satisfying the contract.
